note: Depth modules at the level of job-posting titles. They add no new axes: `core_ref` points to the Core's technical domains and role functions. Each role function pairs with one role pack. `differs_from` states in one line how a role differs from its neighbors, and the result reads that line. Items ask about a different judgment for each role

exploration.note: All eight roles can be compared. Rather than asking all fifty-six items at once, the student picks up to two roles of interest after the Core in-depth stage, and the chosen roles are examined in depth from STANDARD. Roles not chosen are compared using the Core's confirmed axes. Choosing a role does not change the Core verdict

packs.owns: Finalizes circuit architecture, component values and operating conditions
decides: Which parts and grades to use

differs_from.line: Analysis is responsible for whether predictions hold; design has the authority to change component values
Process sets the conditions for building it again and again; design decides what gets built

items.ask: Have you been responsible for changing component values and decided them yourself?
Have you delivered a schematic and component selection table that went to fabrication?
Have you decided which of several conflicting requirements to prioritize?
Have you decided whether to give up efficiency or size?
Have you put two design options against the same criteria and picked one?
Have you changed component values because a circuit did not work as intended?
Has a board ever been built from a schematic you delivered?

application_material: A set of schematics and component selection tables
Design calculations
A one-page note on where you concentrated the margins

packs.owns: Predicts before anything is built and is responsible for whether those predictions hold
decides: Which models and simplifications to use
How far the results can be trusted

differs_from.line: Design has the authority to change component values; analysis is responsible for whether predictions are right
Testing judges what has been built; analysis predicts before it is built

items.ask: Have you set up the simulation mesh and boundary conditions yourself?
Have you matched simulation results with measurements and written down why they differed?
Did you decide yourself how far to simplify the model?
Have you left an analysis report that the next person could rerun?
Have you turned the question an analysis had to answer into numerical conditions?
Have you redone the setup because an analysis was far from reality?
Have your analysis results been used as the basis for a design change?

application_material: A report stating the analysis model and conditions
A table comparing results with measurements
A one-page note on how far the results can be trusted and where they stop

packs.owns: Responsible for whether a single verdict can be reproduced

differs_from.line: Quality assures that the verdict holds through mass production and the whole service life; testing judges one case
Analysis predicts before it is built; testing judges from what has been built

items.ask: Have you made a judgment from the spread of repeated measurements?
Have you left a test procedure that someone else could follow exactly?
Did you set the threshold between pass and fail yourself?
Have you chosen the measurement equipment yourself after checking calibration certificates?
Have you decided yourself under what conditions to retest?
Have you turned the test items in a standard into measurement conditions?
Have test results you produced been used in a release decision?

application_material: A set of test plans and test reports
Uncertainty budget
A one-page note on the conditions used for retesting

packs.owns: Finalizes process conditions so the same result comes out every time

differs_from.line: Design decides what to build; process makes every unit come out the same
Maintenance keeps the equipment running; process is responsible for the quality of what comes out

items.ask: Have you changed process parameters yourself based on yield?
Have you calculated and compared defect rates before and after changing conditions?
Have you left a settings sheet that operators could follow exactly?
Have you set and written down numerical control limits for mass production?
Have you changed a process so the same defect would not happen again?
Have you collected inspection data, looked at the trend and adjusted conditions?
Have conditions you set been applied unchanged on a production line?

application_material: Process recipe sheet
A table comparing defect rates before and after a change
A one-page note on the action that stopped a recurring defect

packs.owns: Finalizes operating and inspection criteria so equipment does not stop

differs_from.line: Process is responsible for the quality of what comes out; maintenance is responsible for how long the equipment stays up
Testing judges one case; maintenance keeps the same equipment running for a long time

items.ask: Did you set inspection intervals and replacement criteria yourself?
Have you narrowed the cause of a failure down to equipment or settings?
Have you judged the condition of equipment from operating data?
Have you left inspection records that the next shift could read?
Have you set and written down numerical operating limits?
Have you collected remote monitoring data and looked for signs before a shutdown?
Has a maintenance judgment you raised been used in a decision to replace equipment?

application_material: A table of inspection criteria and intervals
Failure history and action records
A one-page note on operating limits and their basis

packs.owns: Brings many people's decisions together and finalizes requirements and schedules

differs_from.line: Design settles one block in depth; planning resolves mismatches between blocks
Maintenance looks after equipment already running; planning sets the scope of what does not exist yet

items.ask: Have you set priorities among conflicting requirements and gotten agreement?
Has a requirements definition you put together become the working basis for several teams?
Did you decide yourself what to cut and what to keep within the schedule?
Have you kept a change history so it was clear later who changed what and why?
Have you checked whether conditions between blocks were inconsistent?
Have you narrowed down why a schedule slipped and reset the scope?
Have you split what to cover from what to leave out when there was no scope yet?

application_material: A one-page requirements definition with priorities
Change history
A table reconciling the conditions between blocks

packs.owns: Narrows down problems with no answer yet and establishes the methods to use
decides: What to hold fixed and what to vary

differs_from.line: Analysis predicts problems that have a spec; advanced development builds methods when there is no spec
Design delivers one buildable solution; advanced development first decides whether it can work at all

items.ask: Have you narrowed down and set the question to address when there was no answer?
Have you built a method yourself because none existed?
Have you set an assumption and written down the conditions under which it breaks?
Have you left your methods and conditions so others could rerun them?
Did you find where experimental and calculated values disagreed and write down why?
Did you draw the line where a proposed approach stops holding up, and write it down?
Have your results gone into a project report, a patent or a prototype?

application_material: A report stating the question, assumptions and limits
A document describing the methods and conditions
A table comparing results with values obtained by another method

packs.owns: Assures that requirements hold through mass production and over the product's life

differs_from.line: Testing judges one case; quality assures mass production and the whole service life
Process sets the conditions; quality checks that those conditions are kept

items.ask: Have you judged from production data trends whether the criteria were exceeded?
Has a verdict you gave ever stopped or released a shipment?
Did you set accelerated conditions and lifetime criteria yourself?
Have you decided on and confirmed actions to keep the same defect from recurring?
Have you recorded corrective actions so they could be traced?
Have you turned customer requirements into internal quality criteria?
Have you collected defect data and sorted the candidate causes?

application_material: A table of quality criteria and the basis for verdicts
Corrective action records
A one-page note on the accelerated conditions used for lifetime judgment
